mappings.note: Muhavara 'lattu hona': give the meaning and use it in a sentence. LO-55 names muhavare among the fine points of language to notice, LO-60 covers using them correctly in one's own writing. Rejected LO-50, which is for unfamiliar single words looked up in a dictionary.
Muhavara 'hriday par saanp lotna' - meaning plus sentence. LO-55 with LO-60, as above.
Muhavara 'phoole na samana' - meaning plus sentence. LO-55 with LO-60.
Muhavara 'munh mod lena' - meaning plus sentence. LO-55 with LO-60.
Muhavara 'mukh khil jana' - meaning plus sentence. LO-55 with LO-60.
Muhavara 'nyochhavar kar dena' - meaning plus sentence. LO-55 with LO-60.
The effect of losing Sultan on Baba Bharti has to be inferred from his later carelessness; all four options are plausible, so LO-47 rather than LO-46's gist.
Asks which argument supports 'Baba Bharti bhi manushya hi the' - locating the author's reasoning in the text and concluding from it, LO-47.

Names the lesson's vidha. LO-49 is the outcome about reading compositions of various kinds, which genre recognition rests on. NB the key is self-contradictory: the letter given is (C) atmakatha while the explanation states kahani, which is option (B). Key on the value.
The author's year of birth, from the lekhak-parichay - a specific point in the printed material, LO-47.
Sudarshan's real name is stated in the author note. LO-47.
Which other genres the author wrote in - a question about the range of composition types, LO-49. Rejected LO-47, which is about a point of the story itself.
The author's year of death, from the author note. LO-47 detail retrieval.

'kathavastu apne shabdon mein likhiye' - retelling the story in one's own words IN WRITING, which is LO-59 verbatim. Rejected LO-47, which is about locating a point rather than reproducing the whole.
Asks the pupil to write out the dialogue between the two in their own words - LO-59, writing what others said in one's own way. Rejected LO-42, which is the oral version of the same skill.
'kahani ka uddeshya' is the whole text's purpose - LO-46, forming a sense of the composition's vishayvastu, rather than LO-47's specific point.

Invents the conversation that would have followed - LO-44 explicitly names carrying a story forward ('kisi kahani ko aage badhana'), and LO-60 covers doing it in writing with appropriate words and structures. Both cited because LO-44 sits under the oral competency while this item is written.
Asks the pupil to endorse a critical claim about the story with evidence - reading with understanding and offering an opinion, LO-48. Rejected LO-47, which stops at locating points.
Title-justification turns on the whole story's sense - LO-46 rather than LO-47.
'auchitya par vichar kijiye' asks the pupil to weigh a character's judgement - an opinion on what has been read, LO-48.
Baba Bharti's character traits are gathered from the text - locating specific points and concluding, LO-47.
Asks the pupil to argue for a general statement about love from the story - their own comment, LO-48, not LO-47.
'manaviyata ki jeet ki kahani hai' - stating and supporting the story's whole point, LO-46.

Asks the pupil to give the story their own new title and justify it in writing - expressing one's own comment in writing, LO-57. Rejected LO-46, since the answer is the pupil's invention rather than the text's gist.

Write out Baba Bharti's daily routine from the story, with some imagination allowed - setting down another person's expressed experience as needed, LO-56. Rejected LO-59, which is for reproducing what others SAID.
Quote attribution plus the reason behind it - locating the speaker and concluding the motive, LO-47.
How he cared for the horse is described in the text. LO-47.
The kind of joy he felt is given through the story's own comparisons - locating them, LO-47.
His state immediately after the theft is narrated (the cry of fear, wonder and despair). LO-47.
Explains the story's stated message about sacrificing personal loss to humanity - the whole text's point, LO-46.
The change in Khadgasingh's thinking must be traced across the story and concluded - LO-47.
How the disguise was worked is narrated step by step - the sequence of specific points, LO-47.
Explication of a quoted plea - drawing out what it reveals, LO-47. Rejected LO-55, since the line is plain speech, not a muhavara or lokokti.
'kahani ke aadhaar par spasht kijiye' asks for textual evidence that he valued the poor - locating points and concluding, LO-47.
Explication of the narrator's line about loss making him careless of loss - inference from close reading, LO-47.
His reaction when the horse was returned is narrated in the closing scene. LO-47.

'apne samooh mein charcha karke likhiye' - a group discussion about the title, then a written answer: LO-44 covers carrying forward conversation about a composition, LO-46 the sense of the whole story that the title rests on.
The promise Baba Bharti extracted is stated in the text. LO-47.
Whose tears mingled - a specific point in the closing lines. LO-47.
The difference between the two sets of tears is not stated and must be concluded - LO-47.
Where he lived and what he did there - stated details. LO-47.
Who heard of the horse and what sort of man he was - stated details. LO-47.
